stem.text: The tortoise beetle, Chelymorpha alternans, is an insect found in Panama that has several different colour patterns. Fig. 3.1 shows a tortoise beetle.

stem.caption: Fig. 3.1
stem.alt: Diagram of a tortoise beetle viewed from above, with a line labelling the small front shield as 'pronotum, protective outer cover' and two lines labelling the left and right halves of the large rear shell as 'elytra, protective forewings'.

stem.text: Researchers have identified a gene, L, that controls colour pattern in the pronotum and elytra. Gene L has four different alleles: LV, LT, LR and Lr.
Table 3.1 shows five different colour pattern phenotypes of tortoise beetles and their genotypes.

stem.caption: Table 3.1
stem.alt: Table with two columns, phenotype and genotypes, and five rows. rufipennis: a beetle drawing with the pronotum labelled black and the elytra labelled red; genotypes LR LR, LR LV, LR Lr. darien f. militaris-a (dfm-a): a beetle drawing with pronotum and elytra both labelled black and red striped; genotypes LT LT, LT LV, LT Lr. darien f. militaris-b (dfm-b): a beetle drawing with the pronotum labelled black and the elytra labelled black and red striped; genotype LT LR. veraguensis: a beetle drawing with the whole body labelled red; genotypes LV LV, LV Lr. metallic: a beetle drawing with the whole body labelled metallic and red striped; genotype Lr Lr.
stem.note: Table 3.1 is kept as a cropped image rather than a text table because its genotype column is illustrated with small beetle drawings for each phenotype, not plain text.

stem.text: Explain why the inheritance of colour pattern in tortoise beetles can be described as involving multiple alleles.

points.note: A a gene which has more than two alleles

explanation.text: 'Multiple alleles' means more than the usual two alleles of a gene exist in the population. Gene L has four: LV, LT, LR and Lr, which is why inheritance of colour pattern involves multiple alleles rather than a simple two-allele (dominant/recessive) pair.

reasoningChain: Count the alleles of gene L listed in the stem (four).
State that more than two alleles of one gene is the definition of multiple alleles.

inferredMistakes.text: Describing codominance or dominance hierarchy instead of simply stating that there are more than two alleles of the gene, which is what this 1-mark question asks for.

stem.text: A tortoise beetle with dfm-b phenotype was crossed with another tortoise beetle with dfm-b phenotype.
Construct a genetic diagram to show the results of this cross, including the ratio of offspring phenotypes.

points.text: offspring phenotypes dfm-a, dfm-b (×2), rufipennis, linked to genotypes ;

markScheme.note: The MS prints this cross as a vertical genetic-diagram layout (parental genotypes / gametes / offspring genotypes / offspring phenotypes / ratio, each on its own printed line) rather than a drawn Punnett-square grid. The grid above is reconstructed from that layout: both parents are LT LR, so the 2x2 grid of their gametes gives the LTLT / LTLR / LTLR / LRLR offspring the MS lists. Points renumbered 1-5 here for clarity; the MS itself does not number them.

explanation.text: Both dfm-b parents have genotype LT LR (Table 3.1 shows dfm-b has only one genotype). Each parent makes two types of gamete, LT and LR, so a standard monohybrid cross gives offspring in the ratio 1 LTLT : 2 LTLR : 1 LRLR.
Convert each genotype to its phenotype using Table 3.1: LTLT is dfm-a, LTLR is dfm-b, and LRLR is rufipennis. So the offspring phenotype ratio is 1 dfm-a : 2 dfm-b : 1 rufipennis.

reasoningChain: Look up the genotype for dfm-b in Table 3.1: LT LR.
Cross LT LR × LT LR to get gametes LT, LR from each parent.
Combine gametes in a 2x2 grid: LTLT, LTLR, LTLR, LRLR.
Convert genotypes back to phenotypes using Table 3.1 and state the 1:2:1 ratio.

inferredMistakes.text: Treating dfm-b as having a single allele LT (ignoring that Table 3.1 gives it the heterozygous genotype LT LR), which would wrongly predict all offspring are dfm-b.

stem.text: Colour pattern phenotype involves alleles that show codominance. There is also an order of dominance of alleles (dominance hierarchy).
Use the information in Table 3.1 to:

items: list the dominance hierarchy with alleles from the most dominant to the least dominant.

explanation.text: Codominant alleles both show in the phenotype of a heterozygote: dfm-b (LT LR) shows the black pronotum of LT-related phenotypes and the striped pattern, so LT and LR are codominant with each other. The remaining order comes from reading which phenotype appears when each allele is paired with a 'lower' one in Table 3.1: LT and LR together outrank LV, which in turn outranks Lr (the all-recessive metallic phenotype).

reasoningChain: Find the phenotype whose genotype combines two different allele symbols without one simply being masked: dfm-b (LT LR) shows features of both, so LT and LR are codominant.
Rank the remaining alleles by which phenotype 'wins' when paired with another allele in Table 3.1: LT/LR above LV, and LV above Lr.

inferredMistakes.text: Listing LV as codominant with LT or LR, when Table 3.1 shows LV paired with LT or LR produces the LT/LR phenotype (dfm-a or rufipennis), meaning LV is recessive to them, not codominant.

stem.text: Using Table 3.1, deduce the genotypes of each of the parental beetles used in cross 1 and cross 2.

explanation.text: Cross 1 produces a roughly 1:1 ratio of veraguensis to metallic offspring, which fits a test cross between a heterozygous veraguensis parent (LV Lr) and a homozygous metallic parent (Lr Lr). Cross 2 is veraguensis × veraguensis producing both veraguensis and metallic offspring, so both parents must be heterozygous LV Lr (Table 3.1 lists LV Lr as one of veraguensis's two genotypes).

reasoningChain: Look up the possible genotypes of veraguensis and metallic in Table 3.1.
Cross 1's roughly 1:1 ratio fits a cross between heterozygous LV Lr and homozygous Lr Lr.
Cross 2 produces metallic offspring from two veraguensis parents, so both must be the heterozygous LV Lr genotype.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing LV LV for the veraguensis parent in cross 1 or cross 2, which could not produce any Lr Lr (metallic) offspring.

stem.text: An assumption was made that female tortoise beetles have XX chromosomes and males have XY chromosomes. Gene L is not located on the X chromosome. It was concluded that colour pattern phenotype followed autosomal inheritance.
Explain how the evidence in Table 3.3 supports this conclusion.

points.text: there are similar numbers of male and female offspring produced (for each phenotype)
alternatives: if linked to X chromosome no female metallic offspring are produced ;

explanation.text: If gene L were on the X chromosome, a heterozygous mother (XLVXLr) crossed with a heterozygous father could still produce metallic sons (XLrY) but, depending on the father's genotype, metallic daughters would be much rarer or impossible. Table 3.3 shows female metallic offspring (213) at a similar frequency to male metallic offspring (237), which is what autosomal inheritance predicts, not X-linked inheritance.

reasoningChain: Compare numbers of male metallic (237) and female metallic (213) offspring in Table 3.3.
Note they are similar in number, unlike the pattern expected if the gene were X-linked.
Conclude the gene behaves the same way in both sexes, i.e. it is autosomal.

inferredMistakes.text: Describing the 2.9:1 overall phenotype ratio instead of comparing male and female offspring numbers, which is the specific evidence for autosomal (rather than sex-linked) inheritance.

stem.text: Name a statistical test that can be used to determine whether the ratio of observed phenotypes is significantly different from the expected ratio.

explanation.text: The chi-squared test compares observed counts (like those in Table 3.2 and Table 3.3) with the counts expected from a genetic ratio, and tells you whether any difference is small enough to be due to chance or large enough to reject the expected ratio.

reasoningChain: Recall that chi-squared is the standard test for comparing observed and expected ratios in genetics.

inferredMistakes.text: Naming a correlation test (e.g. Spearman's rank) instead of chi-squared; correlation tests compare two continuous variables, not observed-versus-expected counts in categories.

Table 3.1 的 genotypes 列按原文是纯文本，但 phenotype 列每行配有一张小甲虫示意图（标注黑/红/metallic 等部位），无法用纯文本表格呈现，故整张表截图处理，caption 和表头/行义保留在 alt 文字描述里。

MS 3(b) 把遗传图按竖排文字打印（parental genotypes / gametes / offspring genotypes / offspring phenotypes / ratio 各一行），不是画出的 Punnett 方格；按两亲本基因型 LT LR × LT LR 反推出 2x2 方格填入 markScheme.cross，并在 note 字段说明这是重建的，供核对。QP 题干本身也是五条空白填空（parental phenotypes/genotypes/gametes/offspring genotypes/offspring phenotypes/ratio），未印出方格，用一个 answerLines block 的六个 label 表示这组连续填空，这是本次新出现的 stem 写法，供核对是否合适。
